newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens expects new German train orders.
newsitem.headline: Siemens expects new German train orders.

text.p: Industrial group Siemens AG said on Wednesday it expected Germany's railway to place orders this year for new versions of the country's high-speed ICE trains.

The orders from Deutsch Bahn AG would go to a consortium including Siemens' transportation technology unit and Adtranz AG, a 50-50 venture of Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss-Swedish group ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd., Siemens said.
Siemens did not disclose the value of the expected orders, but said they would call for fourth-generation ICE technology that lets trains tilt while taking turns at high speeds.

Siemens and Adtranz were already building 50 trains based on third-generation technology under a contract valued at 1.5 billion marks. These trains were capable of travelling at 330 kilometers per hour and were to begin running along the Rhine between Frankfurt and the industrial Ruhr area by 1999.

In the six months to March 31, Siemens' transportation technolgoy unit saw sales fall 11 percent to 1.6 billion marks, while orders rose 46 percent to 3.2 billion marks. In 1996/97 it had pretax profit of 19 million marks on sales of 4.3 billion marks.

Adtranz in March said it expected 1997 sales to rise to 3.7 billion European Currency Units (ECU), from 3.2 billion ECU in 1996, with profits "much higher" than the 21 million ECU pretax profit reported last year. Orders would rise eight percent to about 4.2 billion ECU.
